output.title: Show HN: schemaguard – TypeScript runtime validation compiled directly from your types
output.body:
schemaguard generates runtime validators from your existing TypeScript types at build time. Instead of writing and maintaining Zod or Yup schemas alongside your interfaces, you keep one source of truth: the types you already wrote.

The compiler plugin (esbuild/Vite) emits tiny, fast validators for API boundaries, forms, and untrusted JSON. It's 2.1 kB gzipped and benchmarks show ~5.5x throughput over Zod on equivalent payloads.

I built this because hand-written schemas drift out of sync with types, causing runtime errors. Three seed-stage startups are using it in production (listed in the README). It's MIT-licensed and currently in alpha (0.4.x), with breaking changes between minors.

Limitations: no Webpack support yet, no dedicated docs site (just README), and no migration guide from Zod. Would appreciate feedback on usability and edge cases in real-world codebases.
